newsitem.title: UK: UK utility stocks up as market picks defence plays.
newsitem.headline: UK utility stocks up as market picks defence plays.

text.p: British utility shares rose as players selected defensive stocks in a depressed market on Thursday, analysts and market makers said.

"When the market's heading downwards, these stocks look relatively defensive and with the downturn over the last few days, there are one or two clear situations where the yield is out of line," said Daiwa utilities analyst, Andrew Stone.

Stone said PowerGen Plc, up 15p to 607p, and Severn Trent Plc, up 12p to 699-1/2p, looked most attractive, with the lowest gearing in the sector making them best placed to withstand a possible windfall tax.

The opposition Labour party has said it will impose a windfall tax should it win the UK general election on May 1 which has pushed utilities stocks below the top of their trading ranges in the last few weeks.
National Power Plc, up 10-1/2p to 489-1/2p, and Thames Water Plc, up 6-1/2p to 666-1/2pp, were particularly strong after news of Indonesian contracts.
Thames is part of consortium which had a contract confirmed on Thursday to build and operate a water treatment plant in Indonesia.
National Power won its first major project in Indonesia as part of a consortium that plans to build a $1.6 billion coal-fired power station.
Investors are looking at overseas earnings as the main area of growth in the future.
